module.title: Constrained differential inverse kinematics with Panda SE(3) workloads
module.expensive_path: Repeated SE(3) residual/Jacobian evaluation, weighted and dense QP objective assembly, joint/velocity inequality construction, QP solve and configuration update. Native-C Windows baseline measures median 146.96 microseconds for one fixed-state 9-DoF solve (five blocks of 1000); separately instrumented 1000 calls spend 59.11 ms in objective assembly and 36.97 ms in inequalities out of 152.93 ms total. These are native investigation timings, not a validated acceleration workload or a target speedup. A meaningful official-example-derived bank of independent target queries or continuous trajectories must be measured and justified in the subsequent task phase; a single tiny QP is insufficient evidence.
module.rationale: These eight files form a 1456-line source-based module spanning robot state, pose/posture objectives, constrained QP construction, solve, and integration. Panda is the principal redundant-arm workload, not the module boundary. The generic APIs include dense-objective fallback, equality hooks, scalar/ball/free-joint handling and native/fallback paths; official tests of those owned behaviors remain in scope even when their fixtures use other robots. Nonunique joint solutions are assessed through task-space and feasibility observables, not equality to one reference joint vector.
excluded: Dedicated collision-avoidance benchmark semantics and contact/dynamics tasks; existing collision/specialist tests that exercise owned or shared behavior still require explicit relevance accounting in the later survey.
Humanoid whole-body control, retargeting, dual-arm coordination and reinforcement-learning training as new task families.
Reimplementation of MuJoCo or DAQP internals; these remain external dependencies whose overhead must be reported.
An actual GPU/accelerator port in this contribution; the deliverable is the task environment and scientific contract.
Final check policies, tolerances and check counts; these await the source gate, survey, calibration and human finalization.
hazards: Upstream sparse checkout is not the full payload: git tree has 772 files / 415770537 bytes. All 26 example Python scripts and the full Panda model were separately fetched and Git-blob-verified for investigation. A source PR must account for its actual payload and all retained licenses.

Panda MJCF has nine scalar coordinates (seven arm joints plus two fingers), not a seven-coordinate model. Any future independent FK/trajectory checker must validate coordinate order, units, body/site transforms, finite values and finger handling.

Official model-backed tests require UR5e, G1, Talos and other assets through robot_descriptions. 262 official cases collected, but only 54 distinct cases have been executed so far; the remaining cases are not claimed passed.

The original Panda convergence function did not attain 1e-4 in one original 20-step call on a phase-zero circular-offset probe. The official documentation scripts execute but do not assert scientific convergence. These are limitations of using smoke results as scientific evidence.

Pose and posture are soft weighted objectives. Keeping the original 1e-2 posture cost can leave a residual floor; 1e-3 with a fixed home anchor and velocity limits converged on the measured reachable targets. This is a proposed configuration, not a finalized tolerance.
The formal variant is numerical-noise calibration. Meaningful q0 perturbation is a separate experiment with the posture target held fixed. No Docker selfcheck or reward record exists yet.

validate.py is stdlib/NumPy-only. Independent FK is feasible and was compared with the pinned full model, but the final validator, malformed-output tests and anti-hardcoding design are not yet authored.
Native optimized code already exists upstream. Python-fallback profiling cannot establish acceleration headroom; CPU native baseline and end-to-end target execution must remain part of the argument.
Docker is not currently on PATH and has not been installed or run; the actual run location/resources must be agreed at the repository's run-plan stop.
